title: The Hive Is Still Paper
thesis: DeepGreen's interesting idea is to bring compute to hard-to-export Cook Inlet energy, but it becomes an Alaska win only if the study proves the engineering and durable local value.
falsifier: This thesis fails if marine output, subsea cooling and maintenance, environmental constraints or the grid path erase the physical advantage, or if the project proves no durable Alaska value beyond its own load.

supporting_facts.fact: The proposal directly couples 66 compute hives to 330 to 350 marine-hydrokinetic turbines with passive cooling.
The notice estimates 100 MW, primarily for the data center; only spare power could reach the Railbelt.
No customer or committed financing is named, and the proceeding concerns study priority rather than construction.

fair_counterpoint: A self-supplied industrial load could create investment and technical capacity without consuming scarce existing generation. The architecture deserves serious study even though no outcome is proven.
stance: Conditionally optimistic about an Alaska-native energy and compute architecture, exact about the burden of proof.

second_movement.recontextualizing_fact: The visual spectacle is still a paper proposal, and its primary power beneficiary would be the compute load rather than the Railbelt.
second_movement.test: Show the proposal's strongest case, then ask it to produce output, cooling, maintenance, grid, financing, customer and environmental evidence before calling it an Alaska win.

runner_up_angles.angle: The public bargain is the story
runner_up_angles.why_it_lost: It assumes a concession fight not established by the notice.
Accurate but too generic to explain why this particular architecture is worth attention.

room_result: Three independent analysts converged after cross-challenge: lead with physical ingenuity, then use the live FERC study process to define the proof that would turn fit into durable Alaska value.
